Sub: Inoperative Accounts - Modalities for payment out of Inoperative
Accounts.

Sir,

In the 190" meeting of CBT, EPF held on 15.09.2010, it was decided that no
interest shall be credited to the account of a member from the first day of its
becoming inoperative i.e. from 37" month. This is to be effective from 01.04.2011.
Copy of Gazette Notification issued by the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Govt.
of India has already bzen circulated by Head Office letter No.
Coord/3(2)2010/Inoperative Accounts/92370 dated 25.01.2011 to all the field offices
of EPFO at Sl. Nd. 465 of the official website.

De For finalising the modalities and to ensure correct identification and
genuineness of the beneficiary alongwith correctness of the amount for
settlement/authorisation of claims out of Inoperative Accounts, an agenda item was
placed before the CBT, EPF in its 192nd meeting held on 15.02.2011 wherein
following modalities/ procedures have been approved: -

a) In all such cases where the establishment is functioning and employer is
available, the attestation of claim forms by the authorized signatory should
be mandatory

b) In those cases where employer is not available to identify the member, the
attestation by the Bank authorities should be insisted alongwith at least
one of the documents as required under KYC (Know Your Customer)
towards identity proof (ID) and proof of residence. These are:

i. PAN Card
ii. Voters Identity Card
iii. Passport
iv. Ration Card
v. ESI Identity Card
vi. Copy of electricity/water/landline telephone bill in the name of
the claimant with the present address.
vii. Driving license, if applicable
viii. Any other identity card issued by the Government authority.

c) A multilevel verifications/counter checking should be done to ensure
correct identification and genuineness of the beneficiary alongwith
correctness of the amount. Taking this into account, following delegation
of power to authorize/settle claims out of Inoperative accounts has been
made: -

i) Account Officer (AO) in charge of Accounts Groups may authorize
claims upto Rs. 50,000/- out of Inoperative Accounts provided
the same is counter checked by another AO.

ii) APFC may authorize claims for Rs. 50,000/- and above out of
Inoperative accounts provided the same is counter checked by
another APFC or in absence of an APFC by an AO.

The above instructions shall be followed scrupulously while settling the cases
out of inoperative accounts. All care shall be taken to reduce the risk of frauds and
to ensure that the claims are authentic and the payments are made to the genuine
claimants.

Yours faithfully,

—

(Rajesn Bansal)
Financial Advisor & Chief Accounts Officer
